title: Golden-prompt cohort sensitivity and peer-referee consensus protocol
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Goal: design and ship a rubric-and-scoring protocol that ties model/config changes to a robust, cohort-aware delta signal that reduces false positives from temperature and prompt variation. We will introduce 'golden prompts' (stable reference prompts per cohort), a sensitivity metric that measures the smallest config change needed to flip score buckets, and a peer-referee consensus stage where a small ensemble of referee models and a human-review sampler adjudicate borderline regressions. The protocol should: 1) be provably less sensitive to generation temperature and stochastic sampling, 2) surface cohort-specific regressions (e.g., long-context, code, multi-turn support), and 3) produce a calibrated delta score that maps to actionable rollout decisions (block, canary, proceed).

Scope: define golden-prompt selection heuristics, cohort definitions and sampling strategy, scoring pipeline changes (include temperature-agnostic normalization + isotonic calibration), referee ensemble composition and weighting, confidence thresholds for automated rollout gating, and dashboard metrics for SRE/PM/Eng reviews. This ticket covers the PM spec, success criteria, rollout plan and artifacts; engineering tickets will implement the evaluator and dashboard work (ENG-2284, ENG-3112).
success_criteria: Aggregate false-positive regression alerts reduced by >= 40% versus baseline over a 2-week A/B
Cohort-level delta sensitivity reproducible in CI: same change yields consistent signal across 3 runs
Automated gate triggers align with human adjudication >= 90% on sampled runs
Documentation and runbook published and linked from Console alerting page
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Spec & Simulation): finalize heuristics and run offline simulation on past 12 weeks of rollouts (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (Canary): enable protocol in evals-harness for internal builds only with canary gating (1 week)
Phase 2 (Shadow): run protocol in shadow alongside existing rubrics for 2 weeks, collect mismatch telemetry
Phase 3 (Automated Gate): enable as gating policy for non-critical configs with human-in-loop for P1 alerts (rollout incrementally)
Phase 4 (Full): replace old delta alerts after 4 weeks of stable metrics and stakeholder sign-off
open_questions: What is the exact size of the golden-prompt corpus per cohort (10, 50, 200)?
Should referee ensemble include a lightweight deterministic ranker in addition to stochastic LLM judges?
How do we weight human adjudication vs. referee consensus when they disagree?
Do we allow separate confidence thresholds per customer tier (hosted vs dedicated)?
decisions: Use stratified cohorts by workload tags (summary, code, multi-turn, retrieval-augmented) rather than purely length buckets
Adopt isotonic regression for final score calibration to preserve monotonicity of delta signals
Referee ensemble = 3 open models (diverse architectures) + lightweight lexical ranker; majority consensus plus tie-breaker human sample
Temperature-agnostic normalization: score from multiple temperatures (0.0, 0.2, 0.6) and aggregate via median to reduce sampling noise
